name: Field Should Not Be Empty
description: You are given a permutation$$$^{\dagger}$$$ $$$p$$$ of length $$$n$$$. We call index $$$x$$$ good if for all $$$y \lt x$$$ it holds that $$$p_y \lt p_x$$$ and for all $$$y \gt x$$$ it holds that $$$p_y \gt p_x$$$. We call $$$f(p)$$$ the number of good indices in $$$p$$$. You can perform the following operation: pick $$$2$$$ distinct indices $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ and swap elements $$$p_i$$$ and $$$p_j$$$. Find the maximum value of $$$f(p)$$$ after applying the aforementioned operation exactly once . $$$^{\dagger}$$$A permutation of length $$$n$$$ is an array consisting of $$$n$$$ distinct integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ in arbitrary order. For example, $$$[2,3,1,5,4]$$$ is a permutation, but $$$[1,2,2]$$$ is not a permutation ($$$2$$$ appears twice in the array), and $$$[1,3,4]$$$ is also not a permutation ($$$n=3$$$ but there is $$$4$$$ in the array).
input_specification: Each test consists of multiple test cases. The first line of contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 2 \cdot 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of the permutation $$$p$$$. The second line of each test case contain $$$n$$$ distinct integers $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$$$ ($$$1 \le p_i \le n$$$) — the elements of the permutation $$$p$$$. It is guaranteed that sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output a single integer — the maximum value of $$$f(p)$$$ after performing the operation exactly once.
approach_summary: Maintain prefix sums and dynamic point updates via Fenwick tree using lowbit operations (i & -i) in O(log N) time and O(N) space.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1905F — Field Should Not Be Empty [70. BIT / Fenwick Tree]
topic_editorial.summary: Point updates and range prefix queries with Fenwick Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every integer $i$ has a unique binary decomposition. Index $i$ in a Binary Indexed Tree stores the cumulative sum of the interval $(i - \text{lowbit}(i), i]$, allowing logarithmic traversal via $i \mathrel{+}= (i \mathbin{\&} -i)$ and $i \mathrel{-}= (i \mathbin{\&} -i)$.
